note: Wednesday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open, after the Tue 28 Jul US close — the day before the FOMC decision (Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET). Risk assets de-risked into the Fed even as the tape ground to records: the S&P +0.21% to a record 7,428.78 and Dow +1.03% to 52,747 on falling oil and strong earnings, but the Nasdaq slipped -0.22% as a global chip rout (NVDA $250B OpenAI-backstop worry) triggered a KOSPI circuit-breaker (~-10%) and Nikkei -4.4%. Metals gave back Monday's bounce (silver -2% to ~$57.5, gold -1.25% to ~$4,030) on a firmer dollar; crypto fell (BTC -2.5%, ETH -3.2%). Sentiment stayed in Fear (baked CNN ~39, crypto ~28 — the dashboard fetches Fear&Greed LIVE in-browser with these as fallback). Breadth is broad but slipping (~66-69% >200-DMA). Flows are the standout: BofA/EPFR (wk to 22 Jul) show a decisive DM→EM/China rotation — China +$21.3bn (record 3rd-largest), EM +$29.6bn (2nd-largest ever), US equities -$7.2bn. CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run, so the 7 sub-components are INFERRED from the composite and cited internals and labeled as such.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index printed a fresh record close (~7,428.78, Tue 28 Jul) above a rising 125- and 200-DMA as falling oil and strong earnings lifted the tape — momentum reads firm/neutral. [Inferred — CNN exposes no numeric per-gauge value this run]

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Participation stayed broad (~66-69% of the S&P above its 200-DMA) but net new highs are narrowing as leadership concentrates — balanced. [Inferred from exchange/Barchart data]

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). NYSE advancers led ~1.19-to-1 Tuesday, but the McClellan Summation has flattened/rolled over since its 8 May peak — the breadth thrust has faded to neutral-with-a-fearful-tilt. [Inferred — mcoscillator/Barchart]

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand skewed hedged into the 29 Jul FOMC and the global chip rout — a fearful tilt consistent with the high-30s composite. [Inferred]

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. VIX closed ~18.2 (-2.5%) on Tue 28 Jul — contained and near its 50-day average, not a panic reading; the least-fearful gauge. [VIX ~18.2 confirmed via Yahoo/Cboe]

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Stocks held near record highs while gold and bonds were mixed pre-FOMC (10Y eased to ~4.62%) — a modestly fearful mix as haven assets drew no decisive bid. [Inferred]

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS ~277bp stayed historically tight (~16th percentile) — credit signals no stress, the most persistently greedy component. [FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 ~277bp, wk to 23 Jul]

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 200-day MA
metrics.value: ~66-69% (68.6% mid-July; ~70% on 18 Jul, 'strongest breadth since 2024/highest since February' per Seeking Alpha; ~66% on 24 Jul per MacroMicro) — a broad majority above trend, a constructive longer-term backdrop that is easing at the margin. 52-wk range roughly 42-70

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
metrics.value: ~57% (Barchart $S5FI ~57.65 on 28 Jul) — above the 50% line, so short-term participation is still positive but the shorter gauge sits well below the 200-DMA reading, consistent with a rally cooling at the margin

metrics.label: NYSE advancers vs decliners (latest session)
metrics.value: ~1.19-to-1 advancers on Tue 28 Jul (S&P constituents; NYSE-composite-specific A/D not cleanly sourced) — mildly positive as the oil-down rotation lifted cyclicals against the semis drag

metrics.label: NYSE McClellan Oscillator / Summation Index
metrics.value: Summation Index has rolled over/flattened since its 8 May peak (+471) — the early-summer breadth thrust has faded; a clean dated late-July Oscillator value was not retrievable from free sources this run (neutral)

metrics.label: 52-week New Highs minus New Lows (NYSE)
metrics.value: Net positive but narrowing — new highs still exceed new lows (Apple, Palo Alto among fresh 52-wk highs mid-July) without a broadening blow-off, matching the flattened Summation (approximate; no precise dated figure found this run)

metrics.label: Cumulative NYSE Advance-Decline line trend
metrics.value: Near highs but flattening — the A-D line held up with the ~67% >200-DMA breadth, but momentum flattened into late July as leadership narrowed toward financials/industrials and away from semis (inferred trend read)

metrics.label: % of 11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA
metrics.value: Estimated ~73-82% (roughly 8-9 of 11 sector ETFs) — Industrials/Financials/Tech firm; only XLK, XLE, XLY negative YTD and Energy the notable laggard after the oil slide; a clean dated count was not extractable this run (inferred from ~67% index-level breadth)

breadth.note: Longer-term breadth is broad but slipping: ~66-69% of S&P members sit above their 200-DMA (down from ~71% intra-July) while the shorter 50-DMA gauge is only ~57% and the McClellan Summation has rolled over since 8 May — indices hold at record highs (S&P 7,428.78) on narrower, cooling participation as leadership concentrates in financials/industrials and semis rout. Several sub-metrics (daily A/D, net new highs, exact McClellan value) are approximate or lagged as labeled. The open question into the 29 Jul FOMC decision: whether a hawkish hold/hike re-tightens or a data-dependent Warsh sustains the grind higher.

flows.period: BofA 'Flow Show' / EPFR week ending Wednesday 22 July 2026 (freshest verifiable weekly; the 16-22 Jul reporting week). Weekly flows lag ~2-6 days; this week PRE-dates the late-week metals/crypto de-risk. Labeled week-to-22-Jul 2026.
flows.narrative: The freshest weekly read (to 22 Jul) shows a decisive cross-border rotation OUT of developed markets and cash INTO emerging markets — above all China, which posted its record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever (+$21.3bn) and drove EM's 2nd-largest weekly haul on record (+$29.6bn) on H2-stimulus optimism, while US equities bled -$7.2bn and Europe -$1.6bn. Cash left money-markets (-$33.9bn) to fund equities (+$30.4bn overall), bonds (+$14.9bn) and gold (+$2.0bn, the largest gold inflow since April) — a barbell that reads as chasing EM/China upside while hedging FOMC-hike and geopolitical risk. Tech drew +$4.0bn (a record $52.8bn over four weeks) and Financials +$1.5bn, and Japan extended its inflow streak to seven straight weeks. Positioning remains the bigger tell: BofA's July FMS shows cash at just 3.6% of AUM (below the 4% contrarian Cash-Rule SELL trigger) with sentiment the highest since February.

regions.note: US-domestic equity funds bled -$7.2bn even as the aggregate global-equity number stayed positive (+$30.4bn) — the money left the US for EM/China. Positioning stays stretched-bullish (FMS cash 3.6%, contrarian sell), leaving the tape vulnerable into the 29 Jul FOMC.
The 2nd-largest weekly EM-equity inflow on record, China-fuelled — the marquee flow of the week and a real bid under the HK-tech core into the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal.

China's record 3rd-largest weekly inflow ever, on stronger-than-expected Politburo stimulus wording and the biggest MLF liquidity injection in five months — corroborates the HK/China-tech bid (Tencent/Alibaba/Xiaomi) even through the semis rout.
A 7th consecutive week of Japan-equity inflows — the persistent DM haven within the rotation, on governance reform and BoJ normalization.
Europe joined the US on the outflow side this week as money chased EM/China — a pause in the 2026 pro-international tilt within the DM complex.

A large money-market OUTFLOW — cash redeployed into equities, bonds and gold rather than hoarded. BofA's FMS cash level (3.6% of AUM) still trips the contrarian Cash-Rule sell signal; parked cash yields ~3.5-3.75% — the book's productive dry powder into a post-FOMC shakeout.

Broad bond-fund inflows continued as investors added duration alongside gold — a hedge against FOMC-hike/geopolitical risk; HY OAS ~277bp signals no credit stress. IG/HY split not separately itemized this run.

The largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April, on the FOMC-hike/Iran hedge bid — even as spot gave back ground to ~$4,030 pre-FOMC. Gold's YTD inflow remains a record; BofA flags a gold 'death cross' and elevated net-longs into the Fed.
